D.t: Angie Nixon trails by 2.9 and wins 30% of simulations. Closing it takes about 130,837 voters switching sides, or 261,674 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +10.2 and D +4.3. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +6.2. Your best recent poll is St. Pete Polls at R +1.7; your worst is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +10.1. 16 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Broward, a projected net 228,914 votes; Orange, a projected net 135,702 votes; Palm Beach, a projected net 79,483 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, D +3.3, 9.2% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +8.0, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +5.4, 5.1% of the vote; Duval, D +11.7, 4.5% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Angie Nixon runs furthest behind in Sumter, Collier, Okaloosa. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 50 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 45 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.32 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 50 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Angie Nixon: Immigration voters 18 to 79, White voters 35 to 63, Midsize counties 37 to 61. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$265K cash against $8.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 40% of the 2,803,021 ballots in Florida so far, against 40% for the other party. That is 5.7 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
